title: Context rot and compaction
summary: Model quality degrades as input grows, often well below the advertised window. Control it by clearing stale tool results, offloading to files, summarising with care and isolating work in sub-agents.
useIf: A run has many tool calls or turns, quality drops late in the run, or you approach the context limit.
avoidIf: Do not compact short tasks, and do not use lossy summaries where exact wording, numbers or constraints must survive.

explain.md: **Context rot** is the loss of quality as input length grows. Chroma tested 18 models and found non-uniform degradation with longer inputs even on simple controlled tasks, and noted that needle-in-a-haystack tests only measure lexical retrieval [[r8]]. Other evidence points the same way: accuracy is highest when relevant text sits at the start or end and lowest in the middle [[r39]], and on RULER only about half of the 17 models tested kept satisfactory performance at 32K tokens despite claiming that length or more [[r33]]. On NoLiMa, 11 of 13 models claiming 128K or more fell below 50 percent of their short-context baseline at 32K, and GPT-4o dropped from 99.3 to 69.7 percent [[r22]]. Measure at your own lengths.

explain.title: Escalation ladder for a growing context
explain.alt: Five steps from cheapest to most invasive: clear stale tool results, offload to files with pointers, keep structured notes, compact history with a summary, isolate branches in sub-agents.
explain.src:
flowchart LR
  A[1 Clear stale tool results] --> B[2 Offload to files with pointers]
  B --> C[3 Structured notes]
  C --> D[4 Compact history]
  D --> E[5 Sub-agents with fresh windows]

explain.md: Anthropic calls tool result clearing one of the safest, lightest forms of compaction, and lists compaction, structured note-taking and multi-agent architectures as the long-horizon toolkit [[r6]]. Manus uses the file system as restorable external memory: drop bulky content but keep the URL or path so it can be fetched again [[r7]]. The Claude API offers context editing in beta (header `context-management-2025-06-27`, strategies `clear_tool_uses_20250919` and `clear_thinking_20251015`), and server-side compaction in beta, which replaces older turns with a summary Claude writes [[r30]][[tr15]]. Agent Framework's compaction framework is experimental and applies only to agents that keep history in memory, because service-managed agents such as Foundry agents or the Responses API with `store` enabled already manage context server-side [[tr14]].

explain.title: Compaction is lossy and cache-hostile
explain.md: A summary drops exact wording, numbers and rare constraints, costs an extra model call and rewrites history, which breaks prefix cache reuse for that part. Anthropic found compaction alone was not enough for long coding runs and added progress files and incremental sessions [[r14]]. Keep tool-call and result pairs together when trimming: Agent Framework treats them as one atomic group because dropping one half causes API errors [[tr14]].

whereToUse: Coding and research agents with dozens of tool calls per task
Long chat sessions where early turns lose relevance
Agents that browse or read large files and pages
Multi-hour runs that span several context windows
Cost and latency work on input-heavy workloads

use: Quality or cost degrades as a run grows
Old tool results no longer matter but could be restored
Work branches are independent enough to run in fresh windows
avoid: Summarising exact figures, identifiers or legal text
Compacting so often that cache reuse disappears
Using the largest window as a substitute for trimming
flips: A later step may need old output: offload to a file and keep a pointer instead of dropping it
Facts must survive exactly: store them as structured notes and pin them
One window cannot hold independent branches: use sub-agents and return condensed results

pitfalls.symptom: The agent contradicts a decision from earlier in the run
pitfalls.cause: A summary dropped the decision or its reason
pitfalls.fix: Write decisions to structured notes, pin them in context and summarise only narrative.

pitfalls.cause: A tool call was removed without its result, or the reverse [[tr14]]
pitfalls.fix: Trim whole call-and-result groups and let the framework's grouping handle it.

pitfalls.cause: History rewrites break the cached prefix and each summary adds a model call
pitfalls.fix: Compact at thresholds, not every turn, and keep the stable prefix untouched.

scenarios.title: Long coding run near the limit
scenarios.situation: A coding agent has made about a hundred tool calls. Most results are old file listings and test logs. Quality is slipping and the context nears its limit. The next steps only need the latest test output and the plan.
constraints: Detail is restorable by re-running tools
A plan and progress file exist
unknowns: Is the provider's context editing available?
scenarios.question: What do you apply first?

options.name: Clear stale tool results and keep pointers, update the progress notes, then compact only if still needed
options.why: Clearing is among the safest, lightest forms of compaction, and nothing is lost because tools can be re-run.
options.tradeoff: A later step may need to re-fetch cleared data.

options.name: Summarise the entire history into one paragraph
options.why: It is lossy and can drop decisions and constraints, and it breaks cache reuse for the history.
options.tradeoff: Right when history is mostly chat with little structure and a lossy summary is acceptable.

options.name: Start a fresh session with only the original task
options.tradeoff: Loses progress unless notes and files carry state, which is the harness job.

flips.if: Notes and files hold state reliably
flips.then: Fresh sessions per phase become safe and cheap.
Compact in batches at a token threshold.

scenarios.title: Exact figures must survive
scenarios.situation: A support assistant holds a thirty-turn conversation where order numbers, amounts and promised actions must stay exact. The context is growing and answer quality dips on later turns.
scenarios.question: How do you manage the history?

options.name: Extract exact fields into a structured state object that is always included, and summarise only the narrative
options.why: Exact data stays lossless and the narrative shrinks safely.
options.tradeoff: Needs schema design and a reliable extraction step.

options.name: Free-text summary of the whole conversation
options.why: Summaries paraphrase numbers and drop rare constraints.
options.tradeoff: Fine for casual chat with no exact data.

options.name: Drop the oldest turns after a fixed count
options.tradeoff: Forgets early commitments unless they are pinned elsewhere.

flips.then: Keep full history and skip compaction.
Store the transcript separately and keep a compact working context.

scenarios.takeaway: Compact the prose, pin the facts.

quiz.q: What did the NoLiMa study find about models claiming 128K or more of context?
options: All kept at least 90 percent of baseline at 32K
Context length had no effect on literal matching
At 32K, 11 of 13 fell below 50 percent of their short-context baseline
quiz.explain: NoLiMa tested 13 models claiming 128K or more, and at 32K 11 fell below half of their short-context baseline, for example GPT-4o from 99.3 to 69.7 percent. Degradation was not limited to open models. [[r22]]

quiz.q: Order the context-management techniques from least to most invasive.
items: Offload bulky content to files with pointers
quiz.explain: Clearing results is the lightest and safest. Offloading keeps content restorable. Summaries are lossy and rewrite history. Sub-agents change the architecture and multiply tokens. [[r6]]

quiz.q: An agent using the Responses API with store enabled shows no effect from a client-side compaction strategy. Why?
options: The service manages the conversation state, so client compaction has nothing to compact
The strategy needs a larger window
quiz.explain: Agent Framework's compaction applies to agents that keep history in memory. Service-managed state, such as the Responses API with store enabled or Foundry agents, is handled server-side. [[tr14]]
